Build review · November 1

What changed—and what to test next

First Steps 0.1.4

Completed games show a bold result at 4× size, with a large PLAY AGAIN button. Replay starts a new saved session using the same board mode, opponent and color. MENU replaces HANDOFF. Completed-game panels no longer ask you to move pieces.

Recognition now checks visibility before guessing piece identity, using the existing self-hosted Qwen model. Physical return checks all 64 squares against the saved position. Mismatches name the square, incomplete or stale scans cannot unlock play, and SCAN BOARD retries. Manual checks enter clearly labeled manual mode.

Two-hand rim movement and hidden MOVE BOARD placement are included. No state or pending AI move is replaced during handoff.

Automated checks passed. Real-camera accuracy, scan speed and founder acceptance remain open.

Recognition: measured improvement

10/10 existing fixture cases and 18/18 related variants now match, including covered pawns returning uncertain. Warm two-square requests took roughly 0.35–1.53 seconds, versus the previous Llama result of 5.5–6 seconds with 5/10 mismatches.

Still open: the 64-crop workload took 30.7 seconds. These are six unique synthetic empty/pawn/covered images and related variants—not real-board or full-piece-set accuracy. Cold model startup can still take tens of seconds. No headset acceptance is inferred.

Local host 0.2.0 uses Qwen; Llama remains configurable. No paid API was introduced. The Qwen path is not Meta/Llama hackathon evidence.

General Living Table 0.6.3

Chess and Candy Land remain available. Special-card rewards orbit the raised illustration twice, travel to the destination, then sprout matching scenery. Cards reach discard in two seconds; pawns keep their starting size.

Download general 0.6.3

Installed and launched; that does not establish acceptance of every effect.

Continuity preserves a session already tracked by Living Table. An untracked midgame still requires explicit import of turn and chess rights; the camera cannot reconstruct missing history.

Next headset session

  1. Confirm First Steps 0.1.4 and its fingerprint. Finish a game, check the large result and PLAY AGAIN, and confirm the next game preserves your choices. Record the Quest environment in H01.
  2. Run H03/H05 first: all six piece types in both colors, center and edge squares, occlusion, wrong identities and lighting. Record cold/warm scan times and every misread; confirm ambiguous results never advance the journal.
  3. Run H04/H07/H08/H09: human → AI → human, virtual continuation, then return to real pieces. Test wrong layouts, scan interruption and exact saved-state recovery. Record failures and timing; do not promote synthetic results to headset passes.

Build evidence: FirstSteps-build.txt; BoardPlacement-tests.txt (23); BoardGrip-offset-tests.txt (3); FirstSteps-tests.txt (20 + chess regressions). Reconciliation-tests.txt (33) and Recovery-scene-tests.txt (14) record synthetic/scene checks. The new recognizer passed four host test groups, 10 fixture cases and 18 related variants. Full scans remain slow; they are not yet a frictionless experience. Existing dates below remain planning targets, not completion records.
